name: AI SEO Masterclass - Module 5 Local SEO in the AI Era
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-08

# Summary
"Local SEO is the most defensible moat in search": a real address, real reviews and real reputation are hard to fake, and AI Overviews show local results for about 63% of location queries (per the lesson). The module covers GBP optimization, citations, reviews, local content, NAP, local links and AI Overview triggers.

# GBP optimization framework
1. Foundation: exact registered name (no keyword stuffing), specific primary category plus up to 9 secondary, 750-character description with service and city in the first 250 characters.
2. Photos: 50+ over time (logo, cover, interior, exterior, team, work), monthly uploads, descriptive filenames.
3. Weekly posts (update, offer, event, product) with a hook, 80 to 100 words, CTA and photo.
4. Q&A: answer questions fast.
5. Services/products listed individually with descriptions.

# Citations
Tier 1 core platforms (Google, Bing, Apple Business Connect, Facebook, Yelp, YP, BBB, Foursquare, Chamber), tier 2 industry directories (contractors: Angi, HomeAdvisor, Thumbtack, Houzz, Porch), tier 3 local directories, tier 4 data aggregators (Data Axle, Neustar Localeze, Foursquare/Factual). Audit and fix in order: GBP first, then aggregators, then tier 1, 2, 3.

# Reviews
Reviews are called the #1 local factor. Goal: 10+ new per month at 4.5+ stars. Systems: point-of-service ask, 24-hour email, SMS, review landing page, QR cards, day 1/3/7 follow-ups. Negative review reply formula: thank, acknowledge, apologize without admitting fault, offer a fix, move offline, under 100 words. Review velocity beats total count.

# Local content and links
Service area pages (about 1,100 words: intro, services in city, why locals choose us, nearby areas, 5 to 7 local FAQs, CTA), "best of city" guides, local case studies, local FAQ (permits, cost, timing), community content. Links: local guest posts, sponsorships ($100 to $500), partner pages, resource pages, HARO, local PR, scholarships.

# AI Overview triggers for local
"Best [service] in [city]", "how much does [service] cost in [city]", "[service] near me", "[business] reviews". Answer first, question headings, pricing ranges, current dates, strong E-E-A-T, mobile speed.

# 30-day sprint (condensed)
Week 1 GBP to 100%, week 2 on-site NAP, map embed, service area pages, LocalBusiness schema and 100 citations, week 3 local content and links, week 4 review system.

# How this applies to TAG clients
- GBP is read-only for Claude on Pipeliners and Summit AZ; Scott handles GBP for Alphalete. Recommendations go to Kim/Scott as lists ([Google Business Profile](lib:brain-google-business-profile)).
- NAP consistency must account for intentional call-tracking numbers (Summit GHL DNI, Alphalete WhatConverts DNI, Pipeliners GBP vs source numbers). Do not "fix" those as inconsistencies ([WhatConverts](lib:brain-whatconverts), [GoHighLevel](lib:brain-gohighlevel)).
- The lesson suggests seeding Q&A from other Google accounts and upvoting your own answers; that is against Google policy and not a TAG tactic.
- The city/service page template lines up with TAG city page rebuilds (Pipeliners Avondale layout, Summit city-service pages).
